fases.Phase 1: First test of a drug in people, usually in a small group. The question it tries to answer: is it safe, and what dose can be given without causing serious harm? It does not yet try to prove that the drug works.
fases.Phase 1/2: A study that joins two stages into one. First it answers the phase 1 question (is it safe, and what dose should be used?) and then, with the chosen dose, it starts answering the phase 2 question (are there signs that it works?).
fases.Phase 2: Second stage of testing in people, with a larger group than phase 1. The question it tries to answer: does the drug work in the disease it was designed for, and at what dose? It also keeps checking safety. If results are good, the next step is usually phase 3.
fases.Phase 2/3: A study that joins phase 2 and phase 3 into one. First it answers whether the drug works and at what dose, and then it confirms, in many more patients, whether it works better than the existing treatment. If it goes well, its results can be used to apply for approval.
fases.Phase 2b/3: A study that joins two stages. The 2b part measures more precisely whether the drug works and what the best dose is; the phase 3 part confirms in many more patients whether it works and whether its benefits outweigh its risks. If it goes well, it can be used to apply for approval.
fases.Phase 3: The largest and most expensive stage of testing in people, often with hundreds or thousands of patients. The question it tries to answer: does the drug work better than the existing treatment (or than no treatment), and do its benefits outweigh its risks? Its results are usually the basis for applying for approval.
fases.Under FDA review: The company has finished its studies and asked the FDA to approve the drug. The question the FDA tries to answer: do the tests show that the drug is safe and works well enough to be sold in the U.S.?
fases.Approved (FDA): The FDA has authorized the drug to be sold in the U.S. for a specific group of patients. The questions are no longer whether it works in a study, but how many doctors use it, whether it can be approved for more patients or diseases, and how it performs in real life. The company often keeps running studies to widen its use.
fases.Approved (China): China's drug regulator has authorized selling it there, but it is not yet approved in the U.S. The remaining question is whether it can be approved in other countries, and for that the company keeps running studies, usually phase 3.

companias.que_hace: Develops and sells cancer drugs, mostly for blood cancers. Olverembatinib blocks BCR-ABL1, the protein that makes chronic myeloid leukemia cells grow, even when the tumor no longer responds to other treatments.
companias.estado: Sold in China for patients with the T315I mutation or who did not respond to earlier treatments. In China it also has lisaftoclax approved, for another leukemia, which received breakthrough therapy designation as a first treatment in October 2026.

hitos.texto: Lisaftoclax added to the list of drugs covered by China's health system
Still enrolling patients in three phase 3 studies of olverembatinib (POLARIS-1, 2 and 3)

items: POLARIS-1, MRD-negative complete response rate: above 60% at best, in the first dataset (company-reported)
POLARIS-2, MMR rate: no results reported yet

companias.que_hace: Develops gedatolisib (brand name REVTORPYK), a breast cancer drug that blocks several parts of the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway, a circuit tumor cells use to grow.
companias.estado: Sold in the U.S. for patients with advanced HR+/HER2- breast cancer without a PIK3CA mutation. In October 2026 it presented data from the group with that mutation: with the three-drug combination that includes gedatolisib, 59% of patients responded, versus 33% with alpelisib and fulvestrant.

hitos.texto: Phase 3 study VIKTORIA-2, as a first treatment, is still ongoing

companias.que_hace: Develops drugs that adjust how hard a muscle contracts. Aficamten (brand name MYQORZO) slows a heart muscle that contracts too much and thickens, which makes it harder for blood to leave the heart.
companias.estado: Sold in the U.S. since December 2025 for adults with symptoms, and also approved in China, the European Union and the United Kingdom. In the non-obstructive form of the disease, its ACACIA-HCM study gave positive results.

hitos.texto: Application to the FDA for the non-obstructive form of the disease

items: KCCQ-CSS at week 36: +3.0 points vs placebo (P=0.021)
pVO2 at week 36: +0.67 mL/kg/min vs placebo (P=0.003)

companias.que_hace: Develops drugs for heart diseases. EDG-7500 acts on the machinery that makes the heart muscle contract, to treat hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, in which the walls of the heart become too thick.
companias.estado: Its phase 2 study CIRRUS-HCM gave positive results in June 2026. In July 2026 it sold its muscular dystrophy business to Servier and received US$1.55 billion in cash.

hitos.texto: Start of the phase 3 study of EDG-7500
Start of a phase 2 study of EDG-15400 in heart failure

items: Safety and tolerability: no numeric result reported

companias.que_hace: Develops PIKTOR, a combination of two pills (serabelisib and sapanisertib) that blocks the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway at two different points, for endometrial and breast cancer. It used to be called Sensei Biotherapeutics.
companias.estado: Not approved yet. It has FDA Fast Track designation in advanced endometrial cancer; in October 2026 it showed data in mice with breast cancer, where it slowed the tumor as much as or more than gedatolisib.

hitos.texto: First results (topline) of the phase 2 study in endometrial cancer
Interim data from the breast cancer study

companias.que_hace: Develops precision cancer drugs. Darovasertib is a pill that blocks the PKC protein, which is switched on by mutations found in almost all melanomas of the eye (uveal melanoma).
companias.estado: It has FDA Fast Track designation in the metastatic disease and breakthrough therapy designation as a treatment before surgery. In the OptimUM-02 study, together with crizotinib, patients went a median of 6.9 months without the cancer getting worse, versus 3.1 months with other treatments.

hitos.texto: Finishes submitting the approval application to the FDA together with crizotinib, as a first treatment

companias.que_hace: Develops cancer treatments. Varegacestat is a pill for desmoid tumors, which do not spread to other organs but grow and invade nearby tissue.
companias.estado: The FDA accepted the application for review in July 2026, and in October the European agency (EMA) validated the application for Europe. In the phase 3 study RINGSIDE it cut the risk of the disease getting worse by 84%, compared with placebo.

companias.que_hace: Develops drugs for heart diseases that have no approved treatment. Danicamtiv aims to help the muscle of a heart that is enlarged and weak because of genetic causes contract with more force again.
companias.estado: In July 2026 it finished enrolling the first group of patients in its KINSHIP-DCM study and is already enrolling for the phase 3 part. It went public in June 2026.

companias.que_hace: Develops gels for rare diseases of the skin and blood vessels. QTORIN rapamycin is applied to the skin in microcystic lymphatic malformations, birth lesions that currently have no FDA-approved treatment.
companias.estado: In October 2026 the FDA accepted the application and granted priority review. It has breakthrough therapy, Fast Track and orphan drug designations; in its phase 3 study SELVA it met all six efficacy goals.

companias.que_hace: Develops cancer drugs and drugs for inflammatory diseases. Casdatifan is a pill that blocks HIF-2α, a protein that drives the growth of the most common type of kidney cancer.
companias.estado: Its phase 3 study PEAK-1 compares casdatifan plus cabozantinib against cabozantinib alone. In data from the ARC-20 study presented in October 2026, with that combination as a second treatment, patients went a median of 14.5 months without the cancer getting worse.

companias.que_hace: Develops zovegalisib (RLY-2608), a pill designed to block only the mutated version of the PI3Kα protein, present in many breast cancers; it is also studying it in vascular malformations.
companias.estado: Not approved yet. It has FDA breakthrough therapy designation; its ongoing phase 3 study is called ReDiscover-2.

Expected start of a new first-line phase 3 study

companias.que_hace: Develops pills against cancers that depend on the RAS protein, a kind of growth switch that stays on in many tumors, such as pancreatic and lung tumors.
companias.estado: Approved in August 2026 for adults who have already been treated or who cannot receive combination chemotherapy, whether or not they have a RAS mutation. The European agency (EMA) has started reviewing it.

Decision by the European agency (EMA)

items: OS (RAS G12-mutant): median about 13.2 months vs about 6.6–6.7 months with chemotherapy (HR about 0.40)

companias.que_hace: Develops drugs for rare diseases that cause extreme hunger and obesity due to failures in the MC4R pathway, the brain circuit that regulates appetite. Setmelanotide (brand name IMCIVREE) is an injection that activates that pathway.
companias.estado: In the U.S. it has been approved for this disease since March 2026, and before that for several genetic obesities. It is also authorized in Europe and the United Kingdom, and it went on sale in Japan in October 2026.

Launch in European countries

companias.que_hace: Develops precision cancer drugs. Vopimetostat blocks the PRMT5 protein in tumor cells that have lost the MTAP gene, and aims to damage the tumor without affecting healthy cells.
companias.estado: In October 2026, combined with daraxonrasib (from Revolution Medicines), 82% of 22 pancreatic cancer patients who had already been treated before responded to treatment. After talking with the FDA, it plans a phase 3 study as a first treatment, against chemotherapy.

companias.que_hace: Develops RNA drugs, which switch off or correct specific genes. WVE-007 switches off the INHBE gene with the goal of losing fat without losing muscle.
companias.estado: In the first part of the INLIGHT study, a single dose reduced total fat and belly fat while keeping muscle. It is now testing it in phase 2a studies, alone and combined with tirzepatide, a drug from the Ozempic family (incretins).

enfermedades.Chronic myeloid leukemia: A cancer of the blood-forming cells in the bone marrow. A genetic change creates an abnormal protein called BCR-ABL1 that tells white blood cells to keep multiplying. It usually grows slowly, and pills that block that protein are the standard treatment.
enfermedades.Breast cancer: A cancer that starts in the cells of the breast. There are several types, depending on proteins on the tumor cells. "HR+/HER2-" means the tumor responds to hormones but does not have the HER2 protein, which is the most common type.
enfermedades.Obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy: A disease, often inherited, in which the heart muscle becomes too thick. In the obstructive form, the thick muscle partly blocks blood from leaving the heart, which can cause shortness of breath, chest pain and fainting.
enfermedades.Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy: A disease, often inherited, in which the heart muscle becomes too thick and stiff. It can block blood flow out of the heart (obstructive form) or not (non-obstructive form), and it can cause shortness of breath and tiredness.
enfermedades.Endometrial cancer: A cancer that starts in the lining of the uterus (the endometrium). It is the most common cancer of the uterus, and it is often found early because it causes unusual bleeding.
enfermedades.Metastatic uveal melanoma: A cancer that starts in pigment cells of the eye (the uvea). "Metastatic" means it has spread to other parts of the body, most often the liver. It is rare and has had few treatment options.
enfermedades.Desmoid tumors: Soft-tissue tumors that do not spread to other organs, so they are not considered cancer in the usual sense, but they can grow, invade nearby tissue and cause pain.
enfermedades.Genetic dilated cardiomyopathy: A disease in which the heart becomes enlarged and weak and cannot pump blood well. In the genetic form it is caused by inherited gene changes and can run in families.
enfermedades.Microcystic lymphatic malformations: Birth lesions made of small fluid-filled pockets in the lymphatic vessels, usually in the skin. They can swell, leak fluid, bleed or get infected. Today there is no FDA-approved treatment for them.
enfermedades.Clear cell kidney cancer: The most common type of kidney cancer. Its cells look pale or "clear" under the microscope. It often depends on a protein called HIF-2α to grow.
enfermedades.Metastatic pancreatic cancer: Cancer of the pancreas, an organ behind the stomach that helps digest food and controls blood sugar, that has spread to other organs. It is one of the hardest cancers to treat, and many tumors have a mutation in the RAS gene.
enfermedades.Pancreatic cancer: Cancer of the pancreas, an organ behind the stomach that helps digest food and controls blood sugar. It is often found late and is one of the hardest cancers to treat.
enfermedades.Acquired hypothalamic obesity: Severe obesity that appears after damage to the hypothalamus, the part of the brain that controls hunger and energy use. The damage can come from a tumor, surgery or an injury, and it can cause constant hunger and fast weight gain.
enfermedades.Obesity: A condition in which the body stores so much fat that it can harm health. It raises the risk of diabetes, heart disease and other problems.
